ai.description: This gecko reaches 12 cm. It is bright green with red spots on the back and a dark lateral stripe. It features a yellow-bordered eye and lacks the red throat markings of similar species.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Phelsuma andamanensis* is uniquely identified by the presence of a distinct, dark reddish-brown stripe running from the nostril through the eye to the ear opening.
ai.habitat: *Phelsuma andamanensis* inhabits the tropical evergreen and deciduous forests of the Andaman Islands, frequently found in coconut palms and betel nut plantations.
ai.behavior: The Andaman day gecko is strictly diurnal, spending its active hours foraging for insects and nectar among the high canopy and trunks of tropical trees.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Phelsuma andamanensis* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding occurs throughout the year, peaking during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Phelsuma andamanensis* is endemic to the Andaman Islands in the Bay of Bengal, occurring from sea level up to approximately 700 meters in elevation.
